title: NYT Games Is Coming to the Big Screen With Screenvision

body_markdown:
Moviegoers across the country will soon be invited to solve puzzles together as part of Screenvision’s cinema pre-show.


The New York Times today announced a collaboration with Screenvision that will bring NYT Games to movie theaters nationwide. Starting this weekend, audiences will be able to play along with puzzles from the NYT Games portfolio as part of Screenvision’s cinema pre-show.


The experience will present some of our solvers’ favorite puzzles on the big screen, inviting moviegoers to solve from their seats, either on their own or together with others, before the answer is revealed.


“What makes New York Times Games special is the conversation its puzzles spark. People compare answers, debate approaches and share the experience with one another,” said Chandra Cooks, executive director of marketing, Games. “A movie theater is a natural place to bring that spirit to life, giving a room full of people the chance to solve, react and connect in the moment.”


This marks the first time NYT Games has created a play-along experience specifically for movie theaters. The content is expected to draw from across much of the Games portfolio, including familiar games and formats such as Wordle, Connections and Bonus Puzzles, a weekly collection of playful twists on NYT Games favorites. The lineup will rotate, and the experience will be refreshed regularly.


“Movie theaters bring people together around shared entertainment, making them a natural setting for the connection and friendly competition that define New York Times Games,” said Geoff Schiller, chief executive officer of Screenvision. “We’re excited to help create a pre-show experience that audiences can actively enjoy together.”


The collaboration builds on The Times’s continued efforts to bring NYT Games to audiences in creative new ways while preserving what makes the experience distinctive: thoughtful puzzles, moments of discovery and the joy of solving together.
